verified_findings.note: AC4 states .nomos/data/ but actual DB path is apps/server/data/nomos.db. Explorer classification FRAGILE is correct.
F230 fix feature added TypeScript project references array to root tsconfig.json. Explorer called SOUND, which is accurate post-fix.

new_findings.description: Terminal WebSocket protocol mismatch: server sends { type: 'output', data } (apps/server/src/lib/websocket.ts:27) but client checks data.type === 'terminal:output' and accesses data.payload.data (apps/web/src/hooks/use-terminal.ts:52-54). Two mismatches: (1) type string 'output' vs 'terminal:output', (2) no 'payload' wrapper in server message. Terminal output will never be displayed in the UI.

evidence.detail: Server sends JSON.stringify({ type: 'output', data }) to terminal WS clients
Client checks data.type === 'terminal:output' — does not match 'output'
Client reads data.payload.data but server message has no 'payload' wrapper
WebSocketClient.onmessage parses JSON and passes raw object to handlers — no transformation layer

new_findings.description: Learning router has no ownership checks. list returns findAll() unfiltered, get/update/delete accept any learning ID without verifying user ownership. Any authenticated user can read, modify, or delete any other user's learnings.

evidence.detail: list handler returns learningRepository.findAll() with no user filter — or findByCategory/findByFeature, both unfiltered by user
get handler returns any learning by ID with no ownership check
update handler modifies any learning with no ownership check
delete handler removes any learning with no ownership check

new_findings.description: Notification markRead and dismiss endpoints lack ownership verification. notificationsRouter.markRead (line 48) and dismiss (line 65) accept any notification ID without verifying it belongs to the calling user's project. Other notification endpoints (list, countUnread, markAllRead) correctly verify project ownership.

evidence.detail: markRead handler accepts any id, no ownership check — contrast with list/countUnread/markAllRead which verify project ownership
dismiss handler accepts any id, no ownership check

new_findings.description: Terminal router has no user isolation. All terminal operations (create, write, resize, kill, list, scrollback) are auth-protected but do not check if the calling user owns the terminal session. TerminalService has no userId field in TerminalSession interface. Any authenticated user can read scrollback, write input, resize, or kill any terminal session.

evidence.detail: create handler spawns a terminal with no user association stored
list handler returns ALL sessions, not filtered by user
write handler accepts any sessionId with no ownership check
kill handler accepts any sessionId with no ownership check
TerminalSession interface has no userId field

new_findings.description: Auto-mode stop, status, setConcurrency, setConfig, getConfig endpoints have no user/project ownership checks. AutoModeService is a singleton — it stores one currentUserId meaning only one user can use auto-mode at a time. Any authenticated user can stop auto-mode, change configuration, or read status regardless of who started it.

evidence.detail: stop handler has no ownership check — any auth user can stop auto-mode
status handler has no ownership check
setConcurrency has no ownership check
setConfig has no ownership check

new_findings.description: Settings router allows any authenticated user to read/write global scope settings. This is likely by design for a single-instance desktop app, but would be a vulnerability in multi-tenant deployment.

evidence.detail: set handler: when scope='global', only verifies project ownership for scope='project', not global
getAll handler: when scope='global', no ownership check — returns all global settings to any user

new_findings.description: Spec router accepts arbitrary projectPath from user input and passes it to SpecService which uses path.join(projectPath, '.nomos', 'app_spec.json') without path traversal validation. FSService has validatePath() for its routes, but SpecService does NOT use it. An attacker can read/write files at arbitrary paths accessible to the server process.

evidence.detail: getSpec accepts any projectPath string — no validation
updateSpec accepts any projectPath and writes files without validation
loadSpec uses join(projectPath, '.nomos', 'app_spec.json') — path.join does NOT prevent traversal
saveSpec writes to arbitrary path with mkdir recursive: true — can create directories anywhere
FSService has validatePath() with proper traversal protection, but SpecService doesn't use it

new_findings.description: AgentService.listSessions() returns ALL sessions globally (sessionRepository.findAll()), and the router only filters client-side. While the agent router does filter by userId (agent.ts:97), and the session router also filters post-fetch (session.ts:91), this is inefficient and fetches data the user shouldn't see even temporarily. AutoModeService is a singleton with one currentUserId — only one user can use auto-mode at a time.

evidence.detail: listSessions calls service.listSessions() which returns ALL, then filters by userId
Session list handler fetches findAll() then filters by userId
currentUserId is a single field — only supports one user at a time

new_findings.description: Kanban board is missing a 'failed' status column. KANBAN_COLUMNS (kanban-board.tsx:40-66) only defines 5 columns: backlog, pending, in_progress, waiting_approval, verified. Features with 'failed' status disappear from the board. A comment at line 35 acknowledges this is intentional, but the state machine supports 'failed' as a valid state.

evidence.detail: Comment: 'failed' is a valid transition target but not shown as a column
KANBAN_COLUMNS has 5 statuses, 'failed' omitted
FEATURE_VALID_TRANSITIONS includes 'failed' as valid target from in_progress

new_findings.description: TanStack Router devtools and React Query devtools are always rendered in production. Both are outside any conditional and will ship to production builds, adding bundle size and exposing internal state.

evidence.detail: TanStackRouterDevtools rendered unconditionally — no import.meta.env.DEV check
ReactQueryDevtools rendered unconditionally

new_findings.description: featureRouter.bulkCreate (feature.ts:197-229) creates features in a sequential for loop WITHOUT transaction wrapping. If the Nth create fails, the first N-1 features are already committed. This results in partial inserts with no rollback. Also, errors are silently caught and returned as { id: feat.title, success: false } with no error detail.

evidence.detail: bulkCreate iterates with for-of loop, each create is independent — no transaction
catch block swallows error, returns { id: feat.title, success: false } with no error message
bulkDelete has the same pattern — sequential deletes without transaction, silent error swallowing

new_findings.description: ID generation uses SELECT MAX(id) + increment inside a transaction with retry logic for UNIQUE constraint violations. While the retry mechanism (3 attempts) handles race conditions, the F/P/S/L prefixed IDs are capped at 999 entries (padStart 3 digits). At F999, the next ID would be F1000 which breaks the F### pattern. No guard exists for overflow.

evidence.detail: padStart(3, '0') — after 999, IDs become 4+ digits breaking the branded pattern
Retry loop with maxRetries=3 handles race conditions, but no overflow check
